numerical_failure.observed_behavior: An object-dtype array of numbers cast with astype to a timedelta64 dtype is read as nanoseconds and truncated, so pd.Series([2, 3], dtype=object).astype("m8[s]") returns [0 days, 0 days] (all zeros).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: The values should be read in the requested dtype's unit, giving [0:00:02, 0:00:03], the same as pd.Series([2, 3], dtype="m8[s]").
trigger_conditions: Input is object-dtype and every non-null value is a number
Target dtype is a timedelta64 dtype with a unit, such as m8[s]
Reached through Series.astype, DataFrame.astype, Index.astype, or Series/DataFrame construction from existing object-dtype data
Input values carrying their own resolution (strings, Timedelta, np.timedelta64) are not affected
oracle_clues: The PR reproducer compares against pd.Series([2, 3], dtype="m8[s]"), which gives [0:00:02, 0:00:03]
The datetime64 branch delegating to DatetimeArray._from_sequence was correct and is the sibling behaviour to match
Numbers such as -2 and 2**40 are expected to match to_timedelta(unit=...)

numerical_characteristics.dtype: object -> m8 (timedelta64) with requested unit such as m8[s] or m8[ms]
numerical_characteristics.precision: unit-level: the requested unit (s, ms) is supposed to apply to bare numbers; the bug read them as nanoseconds and truncated
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: small integers such as 2 and 3 (values 2 and 3 expected as 2 seconds and 3 seconds)
category_specific_evidence: Reproducer: pd.Series([2, 3], dtype="m8[s]") gives [0:00:02, 0:00:03] (correct) while pd.Series([2, 3], dtype=object).astype("m8[s]") gives [0 days, 0 days] (wrong)

Commit: _astype_nansafe object -> timedelta64 branch called array_to_timedelta64 with no unit, read the object array of numbers as nanoseconds and truncated them; the fix delegates to the constructor path as the datetime64 branch already does
Violated property: astype must agree with the constructor, i.e. pd.Series(values, dtype=object).astype("m8[ms]") must equal pd.Series(values, dtype="m8[ms]") (tm.assert_series_equal test)
Test expectation: DataFrame {"a": [2, 3], "b": [4, 5]} with dtype object astype("m8[s]") must equal the same frame built with dtype m8[s]; single-column df[["a"]] path must match the wider block path
Mixed block test: {"a": [2, 3], "b": ["1 sec", "2 sec"]} object astype("m8[s]") must give a=[2,3] read with unit s, unaffected by string neighbour in the same block
Values with strings like "6 sec" mixed with bare number 7 are only read with unit when all non-null entries are bare numbers
Object input with dtype "m8" or "M8" without precision should raise ValueError 'dtype with no precision is not allowed'
reproduction_risks: Fix is per-column conversion for multi-column object blocks; a 2D single-block path can differ from a single-column path
Mixed object content (strings with units alongside bare numbers) changes whether the requested unit applies
Error message for unitless datetimelike targets is produced by the array constructors, not _astype_nansafe; a related merge test message changed to 'Supported timedelta64 resolutions'
